title: The PAT's hourly budget is a shared resource the factory can exhaust
description:
A cloud run failed with:

    GitHub answered HTTP 403 reading .ticfac/runs/<run>/checkpoint.json in pengelbrecht/ticks
    at epic/uzc (0 of the hourly budget left; resets at 1789970415)

That is the PRIMARY limit - 5,000 requests per hour for a personal access token - not the secondary points limit 8xd was about. It was exhausted by a night of runs, most of them before 8xd landed, each reading 1104 tick records per pass and retrying.

8xd removed the per-pass cost (one request instead of 1104), so this should not recur at the same rate. But the exposure is real and worth naming:

- The budget is per TOKEN, shared by every run, every retry and every other use of that token. A run cannot see how much is left before it starts.
- A run that exhausts it fails every subsequent read for up to an hour, and the failures look like unrelated bugs unless the error carries the budget - which it now does, and that is the only reason this was legible.
- A GitHub App installation token would NOT help on its own: also 5,000/hr outside GHEC.

Worth doing:
- Read x-ratelimit-remaining on responses and put it in the run's feed when it falls below some fraction, so exhaustion is visible before it is terminal rather than after.
- Refuse to START a run when the remaining budget cannot plausibly cover it, with the number in the refusal.
- Consider whether retries should back off against the reset time rather than a fixed schedule; Retry-After is already carried.

Found by performing u9h.
acceptance_criteria: A run states the remaining hourly budget when it is low and refuses to start when it is exhausted, naming the reset time
